4º de Primaria · Inglés

Can and can't: abilities

Ficha para imprimir
123456
1

Pregunta de arranquePiensa 30 segundos antes de seguir

Un pez sabe nadar, pero no sabe trepar a un árbol. Un mono sí trepa, pero nada fatal. ¿Cómo dirías en inglés lo que cada uno sabe hacer?

Escribe o di en voz alta tu respuesta. Después .

Con can (poder, saber hacer) y can't (no poder): «A fish can swim, but it can't climb trees». «A monkey can climb, but it can't swim very well». Es uno de los verbos más fáciles del inglés: ¡nunca cambia!

2

Aprende14 apartados

Para empezar: Grandpa's superpowers

Ivan's grandpa is seventy-five years old. Ivan thinks he has got superpowers.

"Grandpa, can you play the guitar?" Ivan asked one day.

"Yes, I can. I can play the guitar and the harmonica. But I can't play the drums. They're too loud for me!"

"Could you swim when you were a boy?"

"Oh, yes! When I was eight, I could swim across the river near my village. But I couldn't ride a bike. We didn't have bikes then."

Ivan was surprised. He can ride a bike very well, but he can't swim across a river.

"What other things can you do, Grandpa?"

"I can cook the best paella in the world. I can tell stories for hours. And I can make a kite with paper and sticks."

"Can you teach me?" asked Ivan.

"Of course! Can you bring me some paper and string, please?"

That afternoon, they made a red and yellow kite. Then they went to the park. The wind was strong and the kite flew very high.

"See?" said Grandpa. "You don't need superpowers. You just need someone to teach you."

Ivan smiled. "I think you are a superhero, Grandpa."

1. What does can mean?

We use can to talk about abilities: things that we know how to do or that we are able to do. «I can ride a bike», «My baby sister can walk», «Birds can fly».

En castellano: can se traduce como «puedo» o «sé»: «I can swim» es «sé nadar». En español usamos «saber» para lo que hemos aprendido (sé leer) y «poder» para lo que somos capaces de hacer (puedo levantar esto). En inglés, para las dos cosas basta con una palabra: can.

2. Can: the same for everybody

The great thing about can is that it never changes. It's the same with all persons: I can, you can, he can, she can, it can, we can, they can. We never say «she cans».

After can, the verb goes in its normal form, without to and without -s: «She can swim», not «She can swims» or «She can to swim». En castellano: el orden es igual que en español: «ella sabe nadar» → «she can swim».

3. Can't: the negative

To say that you are not able to do something, use can't (or cannot, written together): «I can't whistle» (no sé silbar), «Penguins can't fly», «My grandpa can't use the computer».

We often use but to join a positive and a negative sentence: «I can swim, but I can't dive». Pronunciación: en inglés británico, can't suena con una «a» larga («cant»), y can suena más corto y débil. Escucha bien la t final para saber si es afirmativa o negativa.

4. Action verbs

To talk about abilities, we need action verbs. Here are some useful ones: run (correr), jump (saltar), swim (nadar), climb (trepar), dance (bailar), sing (cantar), skate (patinar), ride a bike (montar en bici), play the guitar (tocar la guitarra), cook (cocinar), draw (dibujar), whistle (silbar).

Act them out: one person mimes a verb and the others guess. «You can skate!». Moving your body helps you remember the words.

Vídeo: Action verbs song: What can you do? · Dream English Kids (YouTube) · 10,6 millones de visualizaciones

5. Sports, music and games: play, ride, do

To talk about abilities with sports and music, we need the right verb:

  • play + ball games: play football, play basketball, play tennis, play volleyball. «I can play basketball.»
  • play the + instruments: play the guitar, play the piano, play the drums, play the violin. Notice: with instruments we use the. «She can play the piano.»
  • ride + things with wheels or animals: ride a bike, ride a scooter (patinete), ride a horse, ride a skateboard.
  • do + some activities: do karate, do gymnastics, do judo, do a puzzle.
  • go + -ing: go swimming, go skating, go skiing.

And some more abilities:

  • speak English / Catalan / French
  • count to a hundred
  • stand on one leg
  • whistle (silbar)
  • do a cartwheel (hacer la rueda)
  • touch your toes (tocarte los dedos de los pies)

Be careful: we say play football, not play the football. But we say play the guitar, not play guitar in British English. Ball games: no the. Instruments: the.

6. Questions: Can you…?

To ask about abilities, put Can at the beginning: «Can you swim?», «Can your dog jump high?», «Can they speak English?». We don't need do or does: can is a helper itself.

Short answers: «Yes, I can.» / «No, I can't.», «Yes, it can.» / «No, it can't.». En castellano: «¿Sabes nadar?» → «Can you swim?». Fíjate que solo se cambia el orden: can pasa delante de la persona.

7. Can I…? Permission and requests

Can is not only for abilities. We also use it to ask for permission (pedir permiso) and to ask someone to do something (pedir un favor).

Asking for permission: Can I…?

  • «Can I go to the toilet, please?»
  • «Can I open the window?»
  • «Can I borrow your rubber?» (¿Me dejas tu goma?)
  • «Can I have some water, please?»

Asking for a favour: Can you…?

  • «Can you help me, please?»
  • «Can you close the door, please?»
  • «Can you repeat that, please?»
  • «Can you pass me the scissors?»

How to answer:

  • Yes: «Yes, of course.» «Sure!» «Yes, here you are.» «No problem.»
  • No: «Sorry, you can't.» «Not now, sorry.» «I'm sorry, I'm busy.»

Good manners are very important in English. Always add please at the end of the question, and say thank you when someone helps you. For a more polite question to adults, use could: «Could you help me, please?»

Vídeo: Asking for permission: English dialogue · English Singsing (YouTube) · 637 mil visualizaciones

8. How well? Very well, quite well, a little

We can say how well we do something with these words at the end of the sentence: «I can swim very well» (muy bien), «I can draw quite well» (bastante bien), «I can cook a little» (un poco), «I can't dance at all» (nada de nada).

This is useful to be honest and precise. Nobody can do everything perfectly! En castellano: no digas «very good» para esto: good describe cosas (a good book) y well describe cómo se hace algo (I sing well).

9. Amazing animals

Animals have incredible abilities. A cheetah can run very fast. A kangaroo can jump very far, but it can't walk backwards. A dolphin can swim and jump out of the water. A parrot can talk, a spider can make webs and a chameleon can change colour.

But there are things they can't do: elephants can't jump, snakes can't hear like us and ostriches can't fly, although they are birds. Reto: busca un animal y escribe dos cosas que can y una que can't hacer.

10. Could and couldn't: the past

To talk about abilities in the past, we use could (podía, sabía) and couldn't (no podía, no sabía). Like can, it is the same for everybody, and the verb after it doesn't change.

  • «When I was three, I could walk, but I couldn't read.»
  • «When my mum was six, she could swim.»
  • «Dinosaurs couldn't fly. But some reptiles could fly, like the pterosaurs.»
  • «Fifty years ago, people couldn't send emails.»

Questions: put could first.

  • «Could you ride a bike when you were five?» → «Yes, I could.» / «No, I couldn't.»

Compare now and then:

  • «When I was a baby, I couldn't talk. Now I can talk in two languages!»
  • «Last year I couldn't do a cartwheel. Now I can.»

Pronunciation: the l in could is silent: /kʊd/. It sounds like good with a k!

Animals too! «A baby bird couldn't fly when it was born, but now it can.» «A tadpole (renacuajo) couldn't jump, but a frog can.» Growing up means learning new abilities, for animals and for people.

Ask your family: what could they do when they were your age? What couldn't they do?

11. Reading: our talent show

Read the poster: «Talent Show! Friday at 5 p.m. in the school hall. Come and see our stars! Marta can juggle with five balls. Yusuf can play the violin very well. The twins Leo and Pau can dance hip hop, but they can't sing. Carmen can't dance, but she can tell very funny jokes. And our teacher, Mr Ruiz, can do magic tricks! Can you do something special? Talk to Mr Ruiz before Wednesday.»

Answer: Who can play the violin? Can the twins sing? What can Mr Ruiz do?

12. Let's practise: find someone who…

Play Find someone who… Your teacher gives you a card with abilities: «Find someone who can whistle», «…who can touch their nose with their tongue», «…who can count to 20 in English», «…who can stand on one leg for 30 seconds».

Walk around the class and ask: «Can you whistle?». If they answer «Yes, I can», they show you and you write their name. At the end, report: «Ana can whistle. Pedro can't whistle, but he can stand on one leg». ¡Gana quien complete antes la tarjeta!

13. Joining ideas: and, but

To make longer and better sentences, we can join two ideas with and or but:

  • and (y) joins two similar ideas: two things you can do, or two things you can't do.
    «I can swim and I can dive.»
    «I can't sing and I can't dance.»
  • but (pero) joins two different or opposite ideas: something you can do and something you can't.
    «I can swim, but I can't dive.»
    «Penguins can swim, but they can't fly.»

Notice: we often write a comma (,) before but.

We can also make the sentence shorter if the subject is the same:

  • «I can sing and dance.» (= I can sing and I can dance.)
  • «My sister can read but she can't write.»

Another useful word is or (o), for questions and negatives:

  • «Can you play the piano or the guitar?»
  • «I can't ski or skate.»

When you write about yourself, try to use and and but in every paragraph. Your writing will sound more natural!

Vídeo: Conjunctions and and but · Periwinkle (YouTube) · 505 mil visualizaciones

14. My superhero

Imagine you can create your own superhero. What can he or she do? Here are some ideas for superpowers:

  • fly (volar) and run very fast
  • become invisible (volverse invisible)
  • read minds (leer la mente)
  • talk to animals
  • breathe underwater (respirar bajo el agua)
  • lift a car (levantar un coche)
  • stop time

A superhero always has a weakness (debilidad) too: something he or she can't do.

Read this example:

My superhero is called Captain Wave. She is tall and strong. She has got blue hair and a silver cape. She can breathe underwater and she can talk to fish and dolphins. She can swim faster than a shark! But she can't fly, and she can't stay out of the water for a long time. She cleans plastic from the oceans and helps sea turtles.

To write your profile, include:

  1. The name of your superhero.
  2. What he or she looks like (has got…).
  3. What he or she can do.
  4. What he or she can't do.
  5. How he or she helps people or the planet.

Lo hacemos juntos

Translate: «Mi hermano sabe patinar, pero no sabe nadar».

  1. saber patinar = can skate.
  2. no sabe nadar = can't swim.
  3. Une con but.

Resultado: My brother can skate, but he can't swim.

Make a question: «Your cat can open the door.»

  1. Can pasa delante de la persona.
  2. No hace falta do ni does.

Resultado: Can your cat open the door?

Correct: «She cans dance very good.»

  1. can no lleva -s.
  2. Para decir cómo se hace algo: well.

Resultado: She can dance very well.

Join with but: «Ostriches can run fast. They can't fly.»

  1. One positive idea and one negative idea.
  2. Use a comma and but.

Resultado: Ostriches can run fast, but they can't fly.

Ask for permission politely: you want to use the computer.

  1. Permission: Can I…?
  2. Add please.

Resultado: Can I use the computer, please?

Errores típicos

  • Añadir -s a can: «he cans» → «he can».
  • Poner -s o to al verbo: «can swims», «can to swim» → «can swim».
  • Preguntar con do: «Do you can swim?» → «Can you swim?».
  • Decir «very good» para habilidades: «I can sing very good» → «very well».
  • Escribir cannot separado: «can not» → «cannot».
  • Adding -s after can: «She cans swim».
  • Saying «play the football» or «I could to swim».

Ejercicios (24)

Hazlos en tu cuaderno y después abre la solución.

Nivel básico

  1. Translate: correr, saltar, trepar, silbar.

    Ver solución
    run, jump, climb, whistle.

  2. Complete: «Fish ___ swim.» (sí)

    Ver solución
    can.

  3. Complete: «Elephants ___ jump.» (no)

    Ver solución
    can't.

  4. Complete: I can ___ the piano. (play / ride)

    Ver solución
    play

  5. Complete: She can ___ a bike.

    Ver solución
    ride

  6. Ask for permission to go to the toilet.

    Ver solución
    Can I go to the toilet, please?

  7. What is the past of can?

    Ver solución
    could

  8. Complete with and or but: I can swim ___ I can't dive.

    Ver solución
    but

Nivel medio

  1. Make a question: «You can play chess.»

    Ver solución
    Can you play chess?

  2. Short answer (yes): «Can your dad cook?»

    Ver solución
    Yes, he can.

  3. Short answer (no): «Can they skate?»

    Ver solución
    No, they can't.

  4. Correct: «My sister can plays the piano.»

    Ver solución
    My sister can play the piano.

  5. Join with but: «I can draw.» «I can't paint.»

    Ver solución
    I can draw, but I can't paint.

  6. Write two things you could do when you were five.

    Ver solución
    Open answer.

  7. Write two things you couldn't do when you were five.

    Ver solución
    Open answer.

  8. Ask a friend to help you, politely.

    Ver solución
    Can you help me, please?

  9. Correct: He cans play the guitar.

    Ver solución
    He can play the guitar.

  10. Join: Penguins can swim. Penguins can't fly.

    Ver solución
    Penguins can swim, but they can't fly.

Nivel avanzado

  1. Write the opposite of «very well».

    Ver solución
    not at all.

  2. Write two things you can do and one you can't.

    Ver solución
    Model answer: I can ride a bike. I can swim quite well. I can't play the guitar.

  3. Write a profile of your own superhero.

    Ver solución
    Open answer.

  4. Interview a grandparent: what could they do as children?

    Ver solución
    Open answer.

  5. Write five classroom requests with Can I…? and Can you…?

    Ver solución
    Open answer.

  6. Write a paragraph about your abilities using and and but.

    Ver solución
    Open answer.

Explícalo con tus palabrasComo si se lo contaras a alguien de un curso menor

¿Has nombrado estas ideas?
★

Situación de aprendizajeOur class talent book

The class makes a book about everybody's talents, then and now.

Pasos

  1. Ask your classmates: What can you do? What could you do when you were five?
  2. Write a page about yourself with can, can't, could and couldn't.
  3. Use and and but to join your ideas.
  4. Add a drawing and put all the pages together.

Producto final: A class book of talents.

Cómo se valora

  • Uses can and could correctly.
  • Uses play, ride and do.
  • Joins ideas with and and but.
  • Asks questions politely.

Tarjetas de repasoToca la tarjeta para darle la vuelta

Según cómo respondas, la tarjeta vuelve mañana, en 3, en 7 o en 21 días.

Para familias

  • Jugad a «Can you…?»: cada uno propone un reto (tocarse la nariz con la lengua, silbar) y los demás responden en inglés.
  • Haced una lista de lo que puede hacer cada miembro de la familia, incluida la mascota.
  • Repasad juntos las tarjetas del paso 6 dos minutos al día durante una semana.

Para profesores

Saberes: Expresión de la capacidad con can y can't; verbos de acción; interrogativas y respuestas cortas; adverbios de modo (Lengua Extranjera) (RD 157/2022, segundo ciclo de Primaria).

  • Juego «Find someone who…» con tarjetas de habilidades.
  • Mímica de verbos de acción por equipos.
  • Cartel de un «Talent Show» de la clase en inglés.

Revisado el 22 de noviembre de 2026.

Qué vas a aprender

  • Say what you can and can't do (lo que sabes y no sabes hacer)
  • Use can with all persons without -s
  • Ask «Can you…?» and give short answers
  • Describe the abilities of animals and people
  • Use play, ride and do with sports and instruments
  • Ask for permission and make requests with can
  • Talk about past abilities with could and couldn't
  • Join ideas with and and but and describe a superhero

Palabras clave

can · can't · cannot · Can you…? · Yes, I can · No, I can't · ability · well · action verbs

Tiempo

80 minutos hoy + 2 minutos en cada repaso
